subject: Lumaforge plugin marketplace - indemnity routing and evidence sync
messages:
From: Susan Morales <susan.morales@lumaforge.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Initial MSA redlines — plugin marketplace exposure

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks for the call yesterday. As we scope the Order Form and MSA for the LumaForge integration (we'll be surfacing third-party plugins through your marketplace), our counsel flagged potential exposure for third-party IP claims that originate from partner plugins. Two asks from our side before we proceed to signature: 

1) Clarify indemnity trigger and whether Redwood will accept notice + cure + defend for claims that arise solely from partner-supplied plugins.
2) Evidence and preservation requirements for chain-of-custody when we request assistance (logs, plugin manifest, developer contact).

We'd like to avoid a broad carve-in that would make LumaForge accept responsibility for downstream plugin code we didn't author, but we also want a practical path if an infringement demand targets a plugin discovered via Redwood.

I've attached a short vendor-side risk memo (attachment: plugin_evidence_memo.pdf) and can share our outside counsel's proposed edits — but wanted to surface first to the Redwood legal/commercial team.

Can you confirm who on your side should receive formal redlines?

Thanks,
Susan
Legal Ops — Lumaforge

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.inference.com>
To: Susan Morales <susan.morales@lumaforge.com>

Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MSA redlines — plugin marketplace exposure

Susan —

Appreciate the note and the memo — useful framing. For formal redlines, please send to this thread and we'll route to legal ops (Kimberly) and commercial (Ben) for the deal lane. Quick answers up front: 

- Primary contact for redlines: kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com (legal ops)
- We expect to rely on a defend-and-settle approach for third-party claims where Redwood's runtime or marketplace mechanics are implicated. For plugins authored by a third party, we typically require: notice, opportunity to investigate/cure, and then Redwood (or the plugin publisher) to be given primary defense where appropriate.

Two clarifying Qs that will speed things up on our side: 
1) Do your plugins undergo any code review / signing process before listing? If so, share the checklist.
2) What is the expected evidence retention window for your side (logs, plugin manifests, publisher contact info)?

Ben/Kim — looping you both for redline coordination and to confirm commercial guardrails (cap proposals, insurance offset, and required SLOs for evidence delivery).

If it helps, we can put a 30-minute redline sync on Wed.

-jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>

Quick commercial note: Lumaforge is in our sales cadence for Q3 expansion (see DEAL-9472-LF). They are prioritizing time-to-market for their plugin set so any protracted legal negotiation risks pushing them to a competitor. From commercial: we can be flexible on an indemnity cap for Order Form liability tied to plugin distribution (propose: $1M carveout for third-party plugin claims + insurance requirement of $3M). We'll let Kim lead on exact clause language.

If legal wants to propose a temporary gate (e.g., sandboxed listing until evidence processes proven), that's acceptable to Sales as long as we get a runway to onboard the top 10 plugins in 30 days.

-ben

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>
To: Susan Morales <susan.morales@lumaforge.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MSA redlines — plugin marketplace exposure

Susan / Jasmine —

Attached are proposed redlines (Lumaforge_Redlines_v1.pdf) and a suggested evidence requirements matrix (plugin_ecosystem_matrix.xlsx). Summary of our approach (high level):

- Trigger: Redwood will accept indemnity obligations for third-party IP claims only where (a) the claim alleges infringement by Redwood code or the Redwood-delivered runtime; or (b) a plugin published via Redwood's marketplace includes code that Redwood contributed or modified.
- For third-party-only plugins (no Redwood contribution), we propose: notice + opportunity to investigate + a limited assistance covenant (we will cooperate and provide logs/manifests upon subpoena/court order or mutual agreement).
- Carveouts: AI-generated-output claims and claims arising from customer-supplied training data should remain excluded from Lumaforge's indemnity to Redwood; similarly, Redwood will not accept unlimited responsibility for third-party plugin defects.
- Evidence SLA: 10 business days to turn over plugin manifests and publisher contact details, 30 business days for preserved runtime logs (we'll provide ilog export instructions in the matrix). If expedited — we can commit to 48 hours for triage with an agreed escalation path.

Alternative proposals we included in the PDF: a) cap the Order Form indemnity for plugin-origin claims at $1,000,000, b) require Lumaforge to obtain cyber/tech liability insurance naming Redwood as an additional insured (min $3M), c) include a right of remediation (Redwood may engage the plugin publisher to cure) with cost recovery if the publisher refuses.

Please review and let us know which items are deal-breakers. If Lumaforge's counsel wants to propose specific language on the defend-and-settle mechanics, we'll take a look and mark up.

-kim
Legal Ops — Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- Lumaforge_Redlines_v1.pdf (redlines + two alternative cap options)
- plugin_ecosystem_matrix.xlsx (evidence fields and export steps)

From: Susan Morales <susan.morales@lumaforge.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>, legal@lumaforge.com
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MSA redlines — plugin marketplace exposure

Kim / Jasmine —

Thanks for the thorough packet and the suggested SLA windows. A few items from Lumaforge counsel: 

- The cap proposal ($1M for plugin-origin claims) is in the right direction; counsel is asking whether that cap would apply per claim or in the aggregate across the 12-month term. Can Redwood confirm preference?

- We need clearer language on the "AI-generated output" carveout: Lumaforge wants explicit confirmation that Redwood's indemnity for model outputs does not extend to publisher plugin behavior that alters prompts or post-processes outputs. The redline PDF's current draft is a little fuzzy here.

- Evidence request: our outside counsel has one ask — when Redwood requests retained logs, will Redwood accept hashed/partial manifests for sensitive plugin metadata, with full access upon court order? We can accept that compromise operationally.

Forwarding our counsel's suggested markup inline below for convenience.

On Thu, Jul 1, 2026 at 11:42 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com> wrote:
> Thanks — we've attached redlines and a matrix. See above for the summary.
>
> On triage SLA: 10 business days for manifests, 30 for runtime logs, 48 hours for expedited escalation.

We'll review Susan's inline edits and propose final language for the defend-and-settle paragraph. Can we schedule a 30-min redlines call next Tue (Jul 6) to finalize? If so, Ben, please confirm availability and Jasmine I'll ask Legal Ops to send a calendar invite.

Best,
Susan
